item.title: Cambodia hosts Chinese military for largest Golden Dragon joint exercise yet
item.description:
Cambodia hosts Chinese military for largest Golden Dragon joint exercise yet
Cambodia and China have started joint military exercises aimed at strengthening cooperation between Beijing and its closest political partner in Southeast AsiaBySOPHENG CHEANG Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 6:00 AM
PHNOM PENH, Cambodia -- China and Cambodia launched their eighth joint military exercise on Wednesday, seeking to strengthen ties between Beijing and its closest political partner in Southeast Asia. Cambodian military spokesperson Thong Solimo said the drills are the largest since the exercise began in 2016.
The 15-day Golden Dragon-2026 exercise will end on Dec. 9. Its stated focus is counterterrorism, humanitarian assistance, anti-piracy operations and disaster relief.
The drills are part of Beijing’s broader push to expand its regional influence. Cambodia consistently backs Chinese foreign policy, while Beijing is its most important ally and benefactor. Chinese aid and investment have helped fuel Cambodia’s rapid economic growth in recent decades.
The United States, China’s main rival for influence in the region, has expressed concern over the military ties between Beijing and Phnom Penh. Cambodia suspended its joint Angkor Sentinel exercise with the United States in 2017, after the last drills in 2016. Following efforts by both sides to improve military relations, the exercise is set to resume next February.
Beijing has helped fund an expansion of the Ream Naval Base on Cambodia’s southern coast, raising concerns it could become a strategic outpost for the Chinese navy in the Gulf of Thailand. Cambodia has repeatedly denied any agreement granting China special privileges or the establishment of a foreign military base.

item.title: Pope Leo laments lack of climate commitments after UN talks end without agreement
item.description:
Pope Leo laments lack of climate commitments after UN talks end without agreement
Pope Leo XIV has expressed concern over the failure of United Nations climate talks to reach an agreementBySILVIA STELLACCI Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 5:53 AM
VATICAN CITY -- VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV on Wednesday expressed concern over the failure of United Nations climate talks to reach an agreement, saying that “extreme environmental events linked to the climate crisis are becoming increasingly frequent.”
The pope has embraced defense of the environment in his papacy, taking up one of the core teachings of his predecessor, Pope Francis, whose landmark encyclical Laudato Si (Praised Be) cast care for the planet as an urgent, existential moral concern.
Leo issued an appeal during his weekly audience in St. Peter’s Square to “never forget the human face of the climate crisis, which affects the lives of millions of people, strikes entire communities and undermines the prospects of future generations.”
He called for “fundamental changes in behavior, socioeconomic systems and the governance of our societies,” directing his appeal to “the international community and to each individual.”

item.title: Migration to Spain's Canary Islands breaks day record with nearly 2,000 arrivals
item.description:
Migration to Spain's Canary Islands breaks day record with nearly 2,000 arrivals
Spanish authorities report nearly 2,000 migrants arrived at the Canary Islands on Tuesday, setting a record for a single dayByJOSEPH WILSON Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 5:48 AM
BARCELONA, Spain -- Spanish authorities said nearly 2,000 migrants arrived at Spain’s Canary Islands on Tuesday, a record high for migrants reaching the archipelago on a single day.
The islands located off the coast of West Africa saw a surge in arrivals just before Spain holds a national election later this week, when migration will be a major concern for many voters.
Spain’s maritime rescue service said that 1,990 people arrived on 15 different boats as search and rescue vessels accompanied one dinghy after another to the small island of El Hierro.
“Sadly, this is a historic day,” the Canary Islands' regional leader Fernando Clavijo said in an interview with Spanish radio Cadena Ser.
There were around 100 minors among Tuesday’s arrivals, including a four-day-old baby that had been born during the journey, Clavijo said.
The Canary Islands, a tourist hotspot for many Europeans drawn to its year-round mild weather, have for years been a key entry point for migrants desperate to reach Europe. The route is also extremely dangerous with thousands dying in the attempted crossing.
Although the islands lie about 65 miles (105 kilometers) from the nearest African coast, many migrants take longer routes to evade security forces. The journeys can last days or weeks, with many boats missing their target and drifting into the open Atlantic.
Over 26,000 people have reached the Canary Islands this year, with half that total coming in November. The previous single-day record was hit just two weeks before, when 1,400 people arrived at Gran Canaria on Nov. 7.

item.title: Amnesty calls for independent war crimes probe into Ethiopian shelling in Tigray
item.description:
Amnesty calls for independent war crimes probe into Ethiopian shelling in Tigray
Amnesty International called for a war crimes investigation into shelling by Ethiopian troops and an allied militia in Tigray, saying it verified 14 civilian deaths in four attacksByKHALED KAZZIHA Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 5:35 AM
Share
NAIROBI, Kenya -- Shelling of civilian neighborhoods in Tigray by Ethiopian forces and an allied militia should be investigated as possible war crimes, Amnesty International said Tuesday, as residents near the Eritrean border described military buildups and fears of another war.
Amnesty said it independently verified 14 civilian deaths in four artillery attacks on Alamata between Sept. 26-28, when Ethiopian forces and the allied Tigray Peace Forces advanced on the city.
It also accused forces allied with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front of endangering civilians by establishing military positions in residential areas and schools. The TPLF rejected those allegations in a written response to Amnesty.
The findings come amid renewed fighting in Tigray and growing fears of a wider confrontation between Ethiopia and neighboring Eritrea.
Amnesty interviewed residents, including survivors and medical personnel, and analyzed videos, photographs and satellite imagery.
The Ethiopian government and the military have so far not responded to the report by Amnesty. The human rights group said neither the military nor the allied militia had responded before publication.
Berhe Sibagadis, 41, a father of four in Alitena in Tigray’s Irob district, several kilometers from the border with Eritrea, is preparing to move his family further from the border region with neighboring Eritrea.
“I have to save my family, therefore I have to move to the center of Tigray,” he told The Associated Press by phone.
He said Eritrean forces are occupying a part of his local administration inside Ethiopia's borders.

item.title: 29 miners believed trapped by flooding in an unauthorized gold mine in Indonesia
item.description:
29 miners believed trapped by flooding in an unauthorized gold mine in Indonesia
Rescuers recovered three bodies Wednesday and searched for 23 other miners believed trapped in a flooded illegal gold mine in Indonesia’s West Java provinceByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 2:10 AM
Share
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Rescuers recovered three bodies Wednesday and searched for 23 other miners believed trapped by flooding more than a day earlier in an unauthorized gold mine in Indonesia.
The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the nearby Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in Bogor regency of West Java province.
The shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters (330 feet) deep, is located in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta.
Eleven miners escaped from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, West Java police spokesperson Hendra Rochmawan said. Local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable.
Authorities were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, officials said.
“The problem was that nobody reported it and nobody wanted to report it because the activity was illegal,” said M. Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor disaster mitigation agency.
Rochmawan said police first received reports of trapped miners about 16 hours after the flooding occurred. After an initial assessment by local authorities, firefighters and other agencies, state-owned mining company PT Antam forwarded a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight Wednesday, triggering a full-scale rescue operation.
The search-and-rescue team used submersible water pumps to suck water from the hole and tried to close off openings where groundwater seeped in.

item.title: Bangladesh raises minimum wage for garment workers after weeks of protests
item.description:
Bangladesh raises minimum wage for garment workers after weeks of protests
A government-formed wage board in Bangladesh has raised the minimum monthly wage for entry-level garment workers by 36% to 17,000 takas, or $136, from 12,500 takas after weeks of violent protestsByThe Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 12:47 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
DHAKA, Bangladesh -- DHAKA, Bangladesh (AP) — Bangladesh raised the minimum monthly wage for entry-level garment workers Wednesday by 36% to 17,000 takas ($136) from 12,500 takas after weeks of violent protests that closed factories and disrupted production as workers demanded the minimum wage be doubled.
The workers took to the streets, fought with police and attacked factories for weeks as they demanded better wages and said higher inflation had made their lives difficult.
The garment industry is Bangladesh’s main sector to earn foreign currency through exports, mostly to the United States and Europe. It represents about 80% of the country’s total exports and directly employs about 4 million workers, mostly women from rural areas.
A government-appointed wage board approved the new wage structure early Wednesday after nearly 12 hours of meetings between workers’ and employers’ representatives.

The wage board also revised monthly wages for other workers.

item.title: Malaysia Airlines’ parent to buy 10 Boeing Dreamliners, with options for 6 more
item.description:
Malaysia Airlines’ parent to buy 10 Boeing Dreamliners, with options for 6 more
Malaysia Airlines' parent company has announced plans to buy 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, with options for six more, as part of its fleet modernization strategyByThe Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 12:38 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia -- Malaysia Airlines’ parent company unveiled plans Wednesday to buy 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft, with options for six more, as part of its fleet modernization strategy and expansion into Europe.
The 16 are valued at $9.3 billion before discounts, Malaysia Aviation Group President and CEO Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said. Airlines typically get steep discounts when they buy in bulk.
He said the new planes would bolster the group's competitiveness and support its expansion into Europe.
The first deliveries of the 787-10 Dreamliners are scheduled to begin in 2032, with the initial 10 aircraft expected by 2035, MAG said in a statement. The wide-body aircraft would gradually replace the group's existing seven Airbus A350s, boosting fuel efficiency and providing greater capacity and operational flexibility, it said.

item.title: Spain's economy has grown under Sánchez, but many voters aren't feeling it. 5 charts explain why
item.description:
Spain's economy has grown under Sánchez, but many voters aren't feeling it. 5 charts explain why
Spain's economy is growing faster than most of Europe, but many Spaniards are struggling with high living costsBySUMAN NAISHADHAM Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 10:49 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
MADRID -- Spain's economy has been growing faster than most of its European peers, but many Spaniards haven't felt the benefits. Discontent, particularly around soaring housing costs, is widespread and bound to be a decisive force in Sunday's national election.
On the campaign trail, incumbent Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has had to tread a careful line between boasting about Spain's enviable growth rates while acknowledging voters' frustration over the rising cost of living.
The progressive Spanish leader called an early election for Nov. 29 after weeks of nationwide protests over living conditions, hoping to capitalize on their anger. While Sánchez has warned voters that a right-wing government would not make their lives more affordable, his conservative opponents have slammed his government for doing too little.
These five charts illustrate the disconnect between Spain's economic growth under Sánchez and the financial pressures many voters face.
House prices in Spain rose 43% between 2015 and 2025 when adjusted for inflation, according to Eurostat’s house price index. Across the European Union, prices rose an average of 25% during the same period.
Market pressures and insufficient construction have driven prices even higher in Spain's largest cities and popular tourist destinations, putting homeownership beyond the reach of many young Spaniards.
Spain has a strong tradition of homeownership, but the Bank of Spain estimates the country of 50 million people has a shortage of 750,000 houses based on demand and the pace of new construction.

item.title: North Korea demands closure of Switzerland's new diplomatic office and orders diplomat to leave
item.description:
North Korea demands closure of Switzerland's new diplomatic office and orders diplomat to leave
North Korea has demanded the closure of Switzerland’s new diplomatic office in Pyongyang and ordered the senior diplomat heading it to leave the countryByKIM TONG-HYUNG Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 10:30 PM
SEOUL, South Korea -- North Korea on Wednesday demanded the closure of Switzerland’s new diplomatic office in Pyongyang and ordered the senior diplomat heading it to leave the country within 48 hours.
A day earlier, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, threatened to close the office and condemned Switzerland for imposing sanctions on a youth camp in eastern North Korea over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russia-occupied areas of Ukraine.
The Korean Central News Agency said a senior Foreign Ministry official summoned Astier Sylvain, who heads the Swiss diplomatic office that opened in Pyongyang last month, and handed him a notice demanding the office’s closure and his departure, in protest of the Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children’s Camp. The report said the ministry declared Sylvain persona non grata.
Kim Yo Jong, one of Pyongyang’s top foreign policy officials, described the Swiss sanctions as an “open hostile act” and an infringement of the North’s sovereignty in her statement Tuesday. She claimed that the camp in the coastal city of Wonsan supported “legitimate” cooperation between North Korea and Russia but didn’t directly address Western accusations that some Ukrainian children abducted by Russian forces were sent there to be reeducated.
North Korea has closely aligned with Russia over the war in Ukraine, sending thousands of troops and large shipments of weapons in recent years to support Russian President Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion, possibly in exchange for aid and military technology transfers. item.title: Solomon Islands signs treaty with Australia that checks China's influence in the South Pacific
item.description:
Solomon Islands signs treaty with Australia that checks China's influence in the South Pacific
The Solomon Islands is declaring it will never allow a foreign military base on its soil and rejecting a secretive 4-year-old defense deal with China that raised fears of a Chinese naval foothold in the South Pacific countryByROD MCGUIRK Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 9:37 PM
Share
MELBOURNE, Australia -- The Solomon Islands rejected a secretive 4-year-old defense deal with China that raised fears of a Chinese naval foothold in the South Pacific country and declared Wednesday while signing a treaty with Australia that it would never allow a foreign military base on its soil.
The Solomons’ archipelago is sprawled across the sea route between the United States and Australia, from where U.S. Gen. Douglas MacArthur commanded the Pacific campaign in World War II. U.S. allies fought pivotal battles against Japanese forces on the islands during the war, and the country that today has a population of fewer than 900,000 people remains strategically imperative territory in the U.S. struggle against China for global influence.
The islands' Prime Minister Matthew Wale and his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese signed the bilateral security pact following reports that the Solomons will end its defense treaty with China next year.
The new treaty confirms Australia’s place as the Solomons’ “primary security partner” and states “there will be no foreign military or security base” on the smaller nation 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) northeast of Australia, both prime ministers said in a statement.
The deal is the latest bilateral security pact Australia has struck with Pacific neighbors since Beijing inked a treaty with the Solomons’ previous government in 2022 that created fears the Chinese navy would build a base in the South Pacific.
